title: Payment widget
publishedHtml:
Payment widget is a pop-up form used to enter the payer's card details and email address. The widget automatically determines the type of payment network: Visa, Mastercard, Maestro, or Mir, as well as the issuing bank, and displays the corresponding logos. The form is optimized for all browsers and mobile devices. Inside the widget, an iframe opens that ensures the secure transmission of card details and does not require compliance certification from the merchant. _Widget

Detailed developer documentation: https://widget.cloudpayments.ru/docs/widget.html

Demo of the payment form builder: https://widget.cloudpayments.ru/app/demo

Demo widget

A demonstration of how the Widget works is available in our demo store:

You can use both test card details and real ones for testing. No funds will be debited.


Widget installation

To install the widget, add the script to the head section of your website:

javascript
<script src="https://widget.cloudpayments.ru/bundles/cloudpayments.js"></script>

Warning: Use cloudpayments.js to maintain PCI compliance by ensuring that payment details are sent directly to CloudPayments without affecting your server. Always load cloudpayments.js from https://widget.cloudpayments.ru to remain compliant. Do not bundle the script or host it yourself. _Widget

To display the payment form, register a function to call the pay method by passing either the auth or the charge parameter to it:

json
this.pay = function () {
 var widget = new cp.CloudPayments();
    widget.pay('auth', // or 'charge'
        { //options
            publicId: 'test_api_00000000000000000000002', // ID from the dashboard
            description: 'Payment for goods at example.com', // Payment description
            amount: 100, // Amount
            currency: 'RUB', // Currency
            accountId: 'user@example.com', // Payer ID (optional)
            invoiceId: '1234567', // Order number (optional)
            email: 'user@example.com', // Payer email (optional)
            skin: "mini", // Widget design (optional)
            autoClose: 3, // Time in seconds before widget auto-close (optional)
            data: {
                myProp: 'myProp value'
            },
            configuration: {
                common: {
                    successRedirectUrl: "https://{your website}/success", // Redirection URL
                    failRedirectUrl: "https://{your website}/fail"        // If paid via T-Pay
                }
            },
            payer: {
                firstName: 'Test',
                lastName: 'Testov',
                middleName: 'Testovich',
                birth: '1955-02-24',
                address: 'test drive test home',
                street: 'Lenina',
                city: 'MO',
                country: 'RU',
                phone: '+71234567890',
                postcode: '345'
            }
        },
        {
            onSuccess: function (options) { // Success
                // Triggered on payment success
            },
            onFail: function (reason, options) { // Fail
                // Triggered on payment failure
            },
            onComplete: function (paymentResult, options) {
                // Triggered as soon as the widget receives a response
                // with transaction result from api.cloudpayments
                // For example, calling your analytics
            }
        }
    )
};

Then, call the function in response to an event, such as clicking the Pay button:

javascript
$('#checkout').click(pay);

Notice: The example uses the jQuery library.

A demonstration of how the widget works is available in our demo store:
https://show.cloudpayments.ru

Example of running the widget without jQuery:

javascript
document.querySelector('#checkout').onclick = pay

Embedded JSFiddle:

json
<script async src="//jsfiddle.net/tretyakovsky/xvec6jpb/35/embed/js,html/dark/"></script>

You can use both test card details and real ones for testing. No funds will be debited. _Widget

Parameters

Notice: According to the NSPK requirements, merchant platforms providing telecommunication services (MCC 4814 Telecommunication Services), must provide the payer's phone number. If the phone number is missing from the request, acquiring banks will decline the transactions.

The phone number must be passed in the Phone parameter within the Payer object.

Format: digits only, without delimiters such as hyphens or parentheses.

Example: +71234567890 _Widget

Calling the pay function with either the auth or the charge argument determines the payment processing method:

  • charge for single-stage payments

  • auth for two-stage payments

Parameter

Format

Required

Description

publicId

string

Yes

Website ID, can be found in the dashboard

amount

float

Yes

Payment amount

currency

string

Yes

Currency: RUB/USD/EUR/GBP

accountId

string

Required for subscription creation

User ID

description

string

No

Free-form description of the payment purpose

invoiceId

string

No

Order or invoice number

email

string

No

User's email

requireEmail

bool

No

Requirement to display the user email address field in the widget

data

JSON

No

Any other data associated with the transaction, including instructions for creating a subscription or generating an online receipt, must be wrapped in the cloudpayments object. Reserved parameter names: name, firstName, middleName, lastName, nick, phone, address, comment, birthDate

skin

string

No

Widget design selection. Possible options: classic, modern, mini. Default is classic

retryPayment

bool

No

Displays the "Retry payment" button upon a failed transaction. Default is true

autoClose

number

No

Automatically closes the widget after successful payment following a specified number of seconds, from 3 to 10

payer

object

No

Additional field used to pass payer information: firstName, lastName, middleName, birth, street, address, city, country, phone, postcode

configuration.common.successRedirectUrl

string

No

Redirect URL after a successful non-card payment. For SBP, the value must not exceed 1024 characters, use ASCII encoding, and comply with RFC-3986

configuration.common.failRedirectUrl

string

No

Redirect URL after a failed T-Pay payment

disableEmail

bool

No

Allows hiding the email address field. To hide it, omit requireEmail or set it to false

You can configure the form's behavior for successful or failed payments using the following parameters:

Parameter

Format

Required

Description

onSuccess

Function or String

No

Specify either a function or a website URL. If a function is specified, it will be called after the payment is successfully completed and the user closes the widget. If a URL is specified, the user will be redirected to that page

onFail

Function or String

No

Specify either a function or a website URL. If a function is specified, it will be called after a failed payment. If a URL is specified, the user will be redirected to that page

onComplete

Function

No

Specify a function to be triggered as soon as the widget receives the transaction result response. Redirects are not allowed in this method

Widget language settings

By default, the widget is displayed in Russian. To display the widget in another language, pass the language parameter in the widget initialization settings.

javascript
var widget = new cp.CloudPayments({language: "en-US"});

List of supported languages:

Language

Timezone

Code

Russian

MSK

ru-RU

English

CET

en-US

Kazakh

ALMT

kk-KZ

Recurring payments (subscriptions)

After the payment is successfully completed, the widget can automatically create a subscription for recurring payments. To do this, add several initialization parameters:

Parameter

Format

Required

Description

Interval

string

Yes

Interval. Possible values: Day, Week, Month

Period

int

Yes

Period. Combined with interval, 1 Month is once a month, and 2 Week is once every two weeks. Must be greater than 0

MaxPeriods

int

No

Maximum number of payments in subscription. By default, no restrictions. If you specify a number, make sure it is greater than 0

Amount

number

No

Recurring payment amount. By default, this matches the initial payment amount. If specifying a custom amount, ensure it is greater than 0

StartDate

DateTime

No

Date and time of the first recurring payment. By default, the next payment will occur after the specified interval and period. If specifying a custom date, ensure it is set in the future

CustomerReceipt

string

No

Data for online receipts generation in recurring payments

The parameters for launching recurring payments must be added to the data.CloudPayments.recurrent object, as shown in the example below:

json
this.pay = function () {
    var widget = new cp.CloudPayments();
    var receipt = {
        Items: [// Receipt items
            {
                label: 'Product name 3', // Product name
                price: 300.00, // Cost
                quantity: 3.00, // Quantity
                amount: 900.00, // Amount
                vat: 20, // VAT rate
                method: 0, // Tag 1214: payment method flag
                object: 0, // Tag 1212: payment subject flag
            }
        ],
        taxationSystem: 0,
        email: 'user@example.com',
        phone: '+71234567890',
        isBso: false,
        amounts: {
            electronic: 900.00,
            advancePayment: 0.00,
            credit: 0.00,
            provision: 0.00
        }
    };

    var data = {};
    data.CloudPayments = {
        CustomerReceipt: receipt,
        recurrent: {
            interval: 'Month',
            period: 1,
            customerReceipt: receipt
        }
    };

    widget.charge({
        publicId: 'test_api_00000000000000000000001',
        description: 'Monthly subscription for access to example.com',
        amount: 1000,
        currency: 'RUB',
        invoiceId: '1234567',
        accountId: 'user@example.com',
        data: data
    },
    function (options) {
        // Triggered on payment success
    },
    function (reason, options) {
        // Triggered on payment failure
    });
};

Please note that you can create a subscription by specifying the accountId parameter, which can be an email address, a phone number, or any other payer ID.

For more examples of creating recurring payments from the widget, see the Integration scenarios.

To cancel recurring payments, use the merchant dashboard, the API, or provide the customer with a link to the system's website:

https://my.cloudpayments.ru/

There they can find and cancel their subscriptions independently. _Widget

Mobile widget

The script automatically identifies the user's device and launches the most appropriate widget: desktop or mobile. For the convenience of customers, the mobile version of the widget opens in full screen, allowing them to pay either by card or via one of the alternative payment methods.
